defects: The top reads as a dark, evenly noisy surface with almost no broad reflection pattern from the photographed room.
Support columns, bolts, cable hardware, and edge construction are mostly lost behind the large slab in the matched production views.
The additional mesh count did not translate into materially better perceived source fidelity.
hard_fail_reasons: The production render does not read as realistic furniture at neutral viewing distance.
The photographed glass-and-steel character is not materially approached; the render matches the broad bounding silhouette while missing the visible reflection/material character.
The glass appears materially flat and the support construction remains visually simplified in the production camera.
incumbent_comparison: Compared against desk-v007 in the same production room and matched three-quarter/detail cameras. v009 increases geometry from 19 meshes/4,416 triangles to 136 meshes/38,160 triangles and introduces albedo, roughness, and normal maps, but the production output is visually worse at communicating smoked glass and still hides most manufactured detail. Keep desk-v007 as best-so-far.
likely_causes: The deterministic dark glass albedo and fine normal/roughness variation dominate the broad plane; the Compatibility renderer and room lighting provide little environmental reflection to establish a glass read.
The underside details are occluded by the desk top at the standardized close camera, so raw mesh density is not visible construction quality.
The support geometry uses nested rounded boxes without sufficiently legible material and joint boundaries from the production viewpoints.
next_action_hypothesis: Replace only the procedural dark glass albedo with a recorded source-conditioned glass material map that carries broad subdued window/monitor reflections; keep roughness and normal as separate PBR maps, retain the v009 CAD geometry, and re-render under the identical room cameras. The target is a real glass read from the source photo, not a shader-only polish pass.

observations.art_direction_fit: The CAD construction is more considered than v007, but its in-room appearance still lacks the realistic smoked-glass-and-steel character in the desk brief.
observations.close_up_quality: In run-001 asset-detail.png the broad top resolves as uniform fine noise and black supports; the small join and controller details do not read clearly at the inspection camera.
observations.gameplay_readability: The desk remains legible beneath the two independent monitors and gameplay geometry is unchanged.
observations.geometric_detail: Technical capture reports 136 meshes and 38,160 triangles, but the production images show only a few of the additional support and fastener details.
observations.material_realism: The dark PBR top lacks the broad soft window and monitor reflections visible on the source desk; its actual render reads matte and materially flat.
observations.proportion: The source scene bounds are 66 x 30.01 x 30 inches, within the brief's 0.03-inch height tolerance.
observations.scale_fidelity: Godot measured 66 x 30.01 x 30 inches; no RoomDefinition object or gameplay dimensions were edited.
observations.semantic_recognizability: The production images identify a standing computer desk, though not yet a realistic furniture asset.
observations.silhouette_quality: The broad thin top and paired T supports preserve the photographed desk's general outline.
observations.source_resemblance: The broad silhouette is similar, but the top's window/monitor reflection character and visible finished support construction do not materially approach the photograph.
observations.surface_variation: The render has fine albedo noise but lacks believable glass variation; the noise reads as a uniform material overlay rather than surface character.
observations.technical_integration: desk-v009 loaded through the production resolver as the expected PackedScene; validation passed at 136 meshes, 136 surfaces, and 38,160 triangles.

close_inspection.evidence: The detail render shows a uniform noisy top; most joins, controller components, and fastening detail are not legible at the close camera.

edge_treatment.evidence: The rounded desktop edge and separate laminate strip are visible in profile, though the finish remains simple.

hardware.evidence: Mounting plates and fasteners are mostly occluded from the standardized production angles.

joins.evidence: The production renders do not make the layered column and rail joins legible.

manufacturing_detail.evidence: The photographed desk's visible frame and refined manufactured support details are not reproduced clearly.

material_response.evidence: The rendered glass is dark and matte with little response resembling the broad source-photo reflections.

surface_variation.evidence: Fine noise is present but reads as a uniform overlay, not believable glass or coated-steel surface variation.

thickness.evidence: The 0.72-inch glass thickness is within a plausible manufactured desktop profile.

neutral_viewer_realism.evidence: The matched production three-quarter render remains a broad dark top and largely black supports, not convincing realistic furniture.

photo_character.evidence: Source Sample (2).jpg shows dark reflective glass with broad window/monitor shapes and black T supports; the render only preserves the broad silhouette.

visual_gate.style_evidence: Despite the higher mesh count, the top reads as a large flat dark field and the support assembly remains visually simplified in the actual production render.
